title: Trace-to-determinant identity
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$, where $q=p^a$, and a prime $\ell\neq p$; write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$,
and interpret the $\Qlb$-objects in the
algebraically closed
coefficient category. Let $X_0/k_0$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put
$X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $(\Qlb)_X$ be the constant
Weil sheaf with its canonical Weil
structure. Let $F$ be the
global geometric Frobenius
on the ordinary and
compact-support cohomology of $(\Qlb)_X$, in the
geometric-Frobenius convention. For every
$0\leq i\leq2d$, put

$$
V_i=H^i(X,\Qlb),\qquad F_i=F\vert_{V_i},\qquad
P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_i\mid V_i)\in\Qlb[T],
$$

the data obtained from the
smooth-proper
cohomological family by scalar extension. Let $Z(X_0,T)$ be the
point-count zeta series, and assume
the point-counting trace formula
[cor-trf-point-counting] of the trace-formula chapter for the constant Weil
sheaf. Then

$$
\boxed{
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}(T)^{(-1)^{i+1}}}
\quad\text{in }\Qlb[[T]].
$$

proof.text: Work in $K=\Qlb$, a characteristic-zero field since it extends $\Ql$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. The smooth, proper, geometrically connected, pure-dimension-$d$ hypotheses include the separated finite-type hypothesis through [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]. Apply [prop-cohomological-finiteness] with $E=\Ql$ and the constant Weil sheaf on $X$: the groups $H^i(X,\Ql)$ are finite-dimensional, Frobenius is an automorphism, and these groups vanish for $i\notin[0,2d]$. By [lem-weil-cohomology-scalar-extension-qlbar], for every integer $i$ the isomorphism $H^i(X,\Ql)\otimes_{\Ql}K\simeq H^i(X,K)$ intertwines Frobenius. A finite basis extends to a basis after scalar extension [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]; a zero space extends to zero, and the inverse of Frobenius extends to its inverse. Consequently the $V_i$ of the statement are finite-dimensional, $F_i$ is invertible, and $H^i(X,K)=0$ outside $[0,2d]$. The determinant polynomial under this identification is exactly the statement's $P_{i,\ell}$.

source.place: Proposition 27.3 and Theorem 27.6, pp. 155-156 (finite cohomological range); scalar-extension identification as in the statement of the blueprint item

proof.text: Use the point-counting formula [cor-trf-point-counting] which the statement explicitly assumes for the constant Weil sheaf. Its proper case gives, for every $n\geq1$, $N_n=\#X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F^n\mid H^i(X,K))$. This uses the assumed conclusion of that corollary; no compactification admissibility is inferred from properness. By step 1 all summands outside $0\leq i\leq2d$ vanish, and on $V_i$ the operator is $F_i$, so $N_n\cdot1_K=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F_i^n\mid V_i)$.

source.place: Proposition 27.3, p. 155; Theorem 27.6, proof, second displayed equality, p. 156

proof.text: Let $\varphi:\mathbf Q[[T]]\to K[[T]]$ be coefficientwise inclusion [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map], and set $U=\sum_{n\geq1}N_nT^n/n\in T\mathbf Q[[T]]$. By the defining formula of [sk-def-zeta], which agrees with [def-weil-point-counts-zeta] for this finite-type scheme, $Z(X_0,T)=\exp(U)$. The coefficient-map compatibility [lem-weil-exp-coefficientwise-map] gives $\varphi(Z(X_0,T))=\exp(\varphi(U))$, where $\varphi(U)=\sum_{n\geq1}(N_n\cdot1_K)T^n/n$. Here $U(0)=0$, so the compatibility applies; all integers $n\geq1$ are invertible in the characteristic-zero field $K$. Henceforth $Z$ in $K[[T]]$ means this image, as in the statement.

source.place: Theorem 27.6, proof, first equality, and Corollary 27.8, proof, p. 156 (rational zeta coefficients read in a coefficient field)

proof.text: For $0\leq i\leq2d$ set $A_i(T)=\sum_{n\geq1}\operatorname{Tr}(F_i^n\mid V_i)T^n/n\in TK[[T]]$. In degree $n\geq1$, the coefficient of $\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^iA_i$ is $\frac1n\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i\operatorname{Tr}(F_i^n\mid V_i)=(N_n\cdot1_K)/n$ by step 2, and both constant coefficients are zero. Equality of coefficients therefore gives $\varphi(U)=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^iA_i$, and step 3 becomes $Z(X_0,T)=\exp(\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^iA_i)$. This exchanges only the finite degree-index sum with coefficient extraction.

source.place: Theorem 27.6, proof, third equality, p. 156 (move the inner sum outside)

proof.text: By step 1 each $(V_i,F_i)$ is a Frobenius module in [def-zl-frobenius-trace-series]. Apply the unit's logarithmic identity [lem-zl-log-det-identity] to get $\log P_{i,\ell}=-A_i$, hence $A_i=-\log P_{i,\ell}$. All its hypotheses hold over $K=\Qlb$, including invertibility of $F_i$. To evaluate the exponential of this logarithmic expression, apply [lem-weil-exp-trace-determinant] to the same finite-dimensional space and endomorphism: it gives $P_{i,\ell}\exp(A_i)=1$ and says that $P_{i,\ell}$ is a unit. Substituting $A_i=-\log P_{i,\ell}$ gives $\exp(-\log P_{i,\ell})=P_{i,\ell}^{-1}$. This makes the exponentiation of the unit's log-determinant step explicit, with no semisimplicity hypothesis and no uncited general log/exp inversion theorem.

source.place: Lemma 27.5 and its proof, pp. 155-156; Theorem 27.6, proof, fourth equality, p. 156

proof.text:
Each $A_i$ has constant coefficient zero. Apply the finite-family integer-weight formula of [lem-weil-power-series-exp-hom] with $\varepsilon_i=(-1)^i$ to step 4 and then substitute both identities from step 5:
$$
Z(X_0,T)=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}\exp(A_i)^{(-1)^i}=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}\exp(-\log P_{i,\ell})^{(-1)^i}
=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}(P_{i,\ell}^{-1})^{(-1)^i}
=\prod_{i=0}^{2d}P_{i,\ell}^{(-1)^{i+1}}.
$$
For the last equality, if $i$ is even the factor is $P_{i,\ell}^{-1}$, and if $i$ is odd it is $P_{i,\ell}$. All integer powers are powers of units by step 5. This proves the required equality in $K[[T]]$.

source.place: Theorem 27.6 and its four-line proof, p. 156
